articles.title: Família procura idosa de 82 anos desaparecida em Angra dos Reis | G1
articles.standfirst: Benedita Adão de Souza foi vista pela última vez na madrugada de sábado (24), no bairro Belém.
articles.summary: Benedita Adão de Souza, idosa desaparecida em Angra dos Reis, sofre de Alzheimer e foi vista pela última vez no bairro Belém durante a madrugada de sábado.
articles.body:
Família procura idosa de 82 anos desaparecida em Angra dos Reis — Foto: Reprodução

A família procura por Benedita Adão de Souza, de 82 anos, que está desaparecida desde a madrugada de sábado (24), em Angra dos Reis (RJ).

De acordo com o registro de ocorrência, ela foi vista pela última vez por volta das 4h, caminhando pela Avenida Bom Jesus, no bairro Belém. A movimentação foi registrada por câmeras de segurança de um vizinho. Desde então, ela não foi mais vista.

Segundo a família, Benedita sofre de Alzheimer, condição que aumenta a preocupação dos parentes, já que ela pode ter dificuldade para se comunicar.

A idosa tem cerca de 1,60 m de altura e cabelos brancos. No momento do desaparecimento, vestia um casaco cinza e um vestido laranja com detalhes pretos.

articles.title: Trump oferece US$ 1 milhão por denúncias de fraude eleitoral | G1
articles.standfirst: A uma semana da disputa pelo controle do Congresso, pesquisas apontam dificuldades para o Partido Republicano, enquanto autoridades temem interferência federal no processo de votação.
articles.summary: Trump oferece US$ 1 milhão por denúncias de fraude eleitoral enquanto republicanos enfrentam dificuldades nas pesquisas para as eleições de meio de mandato.
articles.body:
Trump oferece US$ 1 milhão por denúncias que levem a condenações por fraude eleitoral — Foto: REUTERS/Jonathan Ernst

O presidente Donald Trump disse nesta segunda-feira (26) que os EUA ofereceriam US$ 1 milhão a qualquer pessoa que denunciasse uma fraude eleitoral que resultasse em prisão e condenação — a uma semana das eleições de meio de mandato, que, segundo pesquisas, podem ser difíceis para o seu Partido Republicano.

A administração Trump adotou uma postura cada vez mais agressiva em relação à supervisão eleitoral, pressionando estados por dados de registro de eleitores e argumentando que medidas mais rigorosas são necessárias para garantir a confiança pública no processo eleitoral.

Especialistas políticos, autoridades eleitorais democratas e alguns republicanos veem essas ações como uma interferência indevida do governo federal.

"Qualquer pessoa que denuncie fraude eleitoral em eleições passadas, ou na próxima eleição de meio de mandato, receberá US$ 1.000.000 após a prisão e condenação dos responsáveis pela fraude", escreveu Trump na rede social Truth Social, nesta segunda-feira.

Algumas autoridades eleitorais disseram à Reuters que estão se preparando para uma possível interferência federal nas eleições de meio de mandato.

No passado, Trump fez alegações falsas relacionadas a eleições, inclusive ao não reconhecer sua derrota no pleito de 2020.

Seus apoiadores chegaram a invadir o Capitólio dos EUA em 6 de janeiro de 2021, em uma tentativa fracassada de impedir a certificação das eleições pelo Congresso.

Atualmente, os republicanos detêm uma maioria estreita na Câmara dos Representantes e no Senado.

No entanto, às vésperas das eleições de meio de mandato — nas quais o controle do Congresso está em jogo —, a taxa de aprovação de Trump permanece baixa, devido a preocupações dos eleitores com o alto custo de vida e a alta nos preços dos combustíveis.

articles.title: Rodovia entre Tatuí e Boituva é reaberta após deslizamento de terra | G1
articles.standfirst: Trecho na altura do km 25 precisou ser interditado para uma avaliação técnica dos taludes que ficam às margens da pista. Boituva (SP) registrou 85,5 mm de chuva em apenas dois dias.
articles.summary: A Rodovia Gladys Bernardes Minhoto (SP-129) foi reaberta nesta segunda-feira (26). A via estava interditada por deslizamento de terra e árvores.
articles.body:
A Rodovia Gladys Bernardes Minhoto (SP-129), que liga Tatuí a Boituva (SP) e estava bloqueada desde a madrugada de domingo (25) devido a um deslizamento de terra e árvores na via , foi reaberta para tráfego de veículos nesta segunda-feira (26).

Segundo a Defesa Civil, equipes da corporação e do Departamento de Estradas de Rodagem (DER) precisaram ser acionadas e atuaram no local na manhã de domingo. Em apenas dois dias, Boituva registrou 85,5 milímetros de chuva.

Trecho foi reaberto para tráfego — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Tatuí

Imagens mostram galhos de árvores espalhados pela pista. O trecho do quilômetro 25 precisou interditado para uma avaliação técnica dos taludes às margens da rodovia.

Deslizamento de terra na Rodovia SP-129 interditou trecho entre Tatuí e Boituva (SP) — Foto: Defesa Civil de Tatuí

As fortes chuvas que atingiram a cidade causaram estragos além da interdição da via. O Rio Tatuí transbordou na manhã desta segunda-feira e, por isso, a Ponte do Lopesco precisou ser interditada.

A prefeitura afirma que a elevação do nível da água prejudicou o acesso ao local, que fica na zona rural do município. A Defesa Civil está acompanhando a situação na região.

Até a publicação desta reportagem, não havia registro de desabrigados ou feridos.

articles.title: Coronel uruguaio condenado por crimes na ditadura é preso no RS | G1
articles.standfirst: Justiça italiana condenou Pedro Antonio Mato Narbondo à prisão perpétua, convertida pelo STJ em 30 anos por não haver esse tipo de pena no Brasil.
articles.summary: Pedro Antonio Mato Narbondo cumprirá 30 anos de prisão no Brasil após o STJ validar condenação italiana por crimes cometidos durante a ditadura militar.
articles.body:
Pedro Antonio Mato Narbondo foi visto em Maceió, no Alagoas, em 2013 — Foto: Reprodução/Facebook

A Polícia Federal prendeu nesta segunda-feira (26), em Santana do Livramento , o uruguaio Pedro Antonio Mato Narbondo , condenado pela Justiça italiana por sequestro, tortura e morte de quatro cidadãos italianos durante a ditadura militar uruguaia .

Após ser localizado, Narbondo foi submetido aos procedimentos legais e encaminhado ao sistema prisional , onde permanecerá à disposição da Justiça, informou a Polícia Federal.

Conhecido como "El Burro" , Narbondo nasceu no Uruguai e optou pela nacionalidade brasileira nos anos 2000 . Como possui nacionalidade brasileira, ele não pode ser extraditado para cumprir a pena na Itália . Na década de 1970, ele atuava como oficial do Serviço de Informações de Defesa (SID), órgão de repressão política da ditadura militar uruguaia .

Desde março deste ano, por determinação judicial atendendo a pedido do MPF, Narbondo utilizava tornozeleira eletrônica e estava proibido de deixar Santana do Livramento para evitar risco de fuga.

Segundo o subprocurador-geral da República Artur Gueiros, que atua no processo, esta é a primeira vez que um agente de um regime ditatorial cumprirá pena de prisão por violações de direitos humanos cometidas durante a ditadura militar no Brasil .

A decisão foi tomada pela Corte Especial do STJ na quarta-feira (21) e segue parecer do Ministério Público Federal (MPF). Houve a conversão da prisão perpétua aplicada pela Corte de Apelação de Milão para 30 anos de prisão, já que não há esse tipo de prisão no Brasil .

Segundo o MPF, os assassinatos ocorreram durante a Operação Condor, articulação entre serviços de inteligência de países da América do Sul, como Brasil, Argentina, Chile e Uruguai, para perseguir opositores políticos . A operação envolvia práticas como sequestros, transferências de pessoas entre países, desaparecimentos forçados e eliminação de adversários dos regimes de exceção .

Entre os militares ligados ao SID condenados pelas mortes dos quatro italianos, apenas Narbondo permanecia em liberdade.

Durante o julgamento, os ministros discutiram a possibilidade de aplicação da Lei da Anistia, que perdoou crimes políticos cometidos durante a ditadura . A maioria do colegiado rejeitou essa tese .

articles.title: Rodríguez critica volta de Machado à Venezuela: 'Espetáculo' | G1
articles.standfirst: Líder da oposição venezuela retornou ao país neste domingo (26), após um ano de exílio. Marco Rubio, secretário de Estado dos EUA, também comentou a volta e disse que nunca desencorajou Machado.
articles.summary: Marco Rubio, secretário de Estado dos EUA, também comentou a volta e disse que nunca desencorajou Machado a voltar ao país.
articles.body:
A presidente interina da Venezuela , Delcy Rodríguez, acusou María Corina Machado , líder da oposição que estava exilada e retornou ao país neste domingo (25) , de transformar sua volta em "um espetáculo".

Machado, que havia deixado a Venezuela após vencer o prêmio Nobel da Paz e passar meses escondida em meio à repressão do governo Maduro , chegou de surpresa ao país e seguiu de carro até a capital, Caracas , cumprimentando milhares de apoiadores ao longo do caminho.

"O espetáculo poderia ter sido evitado -- os aeroportos estão bem aqui", criticou em declarações na TV estatal nesta segunda-feira (26).

A líder da oposição venezuelana , María Corina Machado, cumprimenta apoiadores — Foto: REUTERS/Gaby Oraa

Antes das declarações mais inflamadas na TV, durante uma visita a um hospital militar em Caracas , ela diminuiu o tom. Afirmou que espera que as negociações com a oposição ofereçam espaço para que todas as vozes sejam ouvidas:

“Espero que o diálogo continue a proporcionar um espaço para a participação política e que aqueles que prejudicaram a Venezuela , aqueles que clamaram por sanções e agressão externa, sintam algum remorso e arrependimento. Espero que tanto o diálogo quanto o programa de coexistência democrática e paz possam proporcionar um espaço onde todas as vozes possam ser ouvidas, onde as vozes que buscam o bem do país possam ser ouvidas".

Após as declarações de Delcy, o secretário de Estado dos EUA, Marco Rubio , também se pronunciou. Afirmou que o governo americano disse, semanas atrás, às autoridades venezuelanas que a líder da oposição deveria ter permissão para retornar sem perturbações e que nunca desencorajou Machado de retornar a seu país.

Sobre a possibilidade de novas eleições presidenciais na Venezuela - já que Delcy está no cargo apenas como interina -, Rubio falou que é necessário que a infraestrutura eleitoral do país seja substituída para que a pleito seja considerado válido.

"Acho que estamos fazendo progressos reais nesse sentido, mas se alguém tentar sabotar esse processo, estará causando um grande prejuízo à Venezuela ", declarou, sem citar nomes.

De acordo com um alto funcionário do Departamento de Estado americano, que falou sob a condição de anonimato à Reuters, os EUA querem que haja um novo Conselho Judiciário Supremo venezuelano até o final do ano, e um novo Conselho Eleitoral logo em seguida.

Rubio também rebateu críticas de Machado ao acordo petrolífero assinado entre os EUA e a Venezuela . Disse que é "um bom negócio, mas Machado tem o direito de criticá-lo".

articles.summary: Vagas de emprego na Baixada Santista contemplam áreas como comércio e construção civil em oito cidades; saiba como se candidatar presencialmente com seus documentos.
articles.body:
PATs da Baixada Santista abrem vagas de emprego diversos - IMAGEM ILUSTRATIVA. — Foto: Reprodução EPTV

Os Postos de Atendimento ao Trabalhador (PATs) oferecem 363 vagas de emprego nesta segunda-feira (26) em cidades da Baixada Santista, no litoral de São Paulo. As oportunidades contemplam diferentes áreas profissionais, incluindo comércio, construção civil, serviços e atividades técnicas.

As vagas são para as cidades de Bertioga , Guarujá , Itanhaém , Mongaguá , Peruíbe , Praia Grande , Santos , São Vicente .

Os interessados devem comparecer presencialmente a um dos PATs, levando RG, CPF e Carteira de Trabalho, física ou digital. Segundo a Secretaria de Desenvolvimento Econômico (SDE), as vagas podem ser preenchidas a qualquer momento, e a quantidade disponível pode mudar ao longo do dia.

Os postos também oferecem serviços gratuitos, como atendimento para solicitação do seguro-desemprego.

articles.title: Eleições 2026 em Uberlândia: Veja a votação por bairro | G1
articles.standfirst: Levantamento mostra os bairros onde Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula tiveram melhor desempenho. Confira a comparação entre o primeiro e segundo turnos em cada localidade da cidade.
articles.summary: As Eleições 2026 em Uberlândia revelaram um mapa detalhado da votação por bairro, destacando o desempenho de Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula em cada região da cidade.
articles.body:
Flávio Bolsonaro venceu em 43 bairros de Uberl enquanto Lula liderou em 16 — Foto: TSE

A disputa presidencial no segundo turno das Eleições 2026 revelou um mapa eleitoral mais dividido em Uberlândia . Embora Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) tenha liderado na maior parte dos bairros com locais de votação, Lula (PT) manteve redutos importantes e alcançou ampla vantagem em algumas regiões da cidade.

O levantamento do g1 com os resultados por bairro mostra como cada região de Uberlândia votou no segundo turno e permite ao eleitor ver a diferença entre o primeiro dia de votação. Confira o mapa mais abaixo.

Apesar de não ter sido eleito presidente do Brasil, Flávio Bolsonoro foi o campeão de votos em Uberlândia , tanto no primeiro quanto no segundo turno .

Confira no mapa abaixo como foi a votação, por bairro, nos dois turnos das eleições 2026 e os locais que apresentaram mudança de votos.

Dos 59 bairros de Uberlândia com locais de votação, Flávio Bolsonaro foi o candidato mais votado em 43 deles . O maior percentual registrado pelo candidato ocorreu no Vigilato Pereira, onde alcançou 70,27% dos votos válidos. Na sequência aparecem Morada da Colina e Gávea, ambos com 67% , além de Fundinho (65,84%) , Tabajaras (65,55%) e Granja Marileusa (64,91%) .

Os números indicam forte concentração do voto bolsonarista em bairros tradicionalmente associados a rendas mais altas, especialmente na região sul de Uberlândia.

Lula venceu em 16 bairros e teve maior força nas regiões oeste e norte

Já Lula foi o mais votado em 16 bairros analisados, no segundo turno. Ele conseguiu virar votos em três locais entre o primeiro e o segundo dia de votação .

O melhor resultado do petista neste domingo (25) ocorreu no Residencial Integração, onde recebeu 66,6% dos votos válidos. Em seguida aparecem Monte Hebron (64,48%) , Pequis (64,06%) e Morada Nova (61,55%) .

Os dados mostram uma presença mais forte do eleitorado lulista em bairros populares das regiões oeste e norte da cidade.

articles.title: American tourist falls 1,000 feet to her death while chasing perfect mountain photo
articles.summary: An American tourist from Miami, Florida, reportedly left a marked trail in the Dolomites, Italy, to take a photo before she fell 1,000 feet to her tragic death.
articles.body: A family vacation in northern Italy ended in tragedy when a 36-year-old American tourist fell down a steep mountain face in the Dolomites, Italy. Michelle Alejandra Rubio Leiva, a marketing and business development professional from the Miami area, died Oct. 17 after stepping off a marked trail, local news outlets reported. Rubio Leiva was hiking near Forcella Pordoi, an alpine pass with an altitude of roughly 9, 000 feet, when she allegedly left the designated path to find a vantage point for a photograph, Italian national newspaper Corriere Della Sera reported. THOUSANDS SWARM STUNNING MOUNTAIN ESCAPE AS SELFIE TOURISM BACKLASH ERUPTS ONLINE She lost her footing and fell an estimated 1, 000 feet down the slope in view of her sister, the outlet said. The hiking group had been close to the upper cable-car station and originally planned to visit the Maria refuge on Sass Pordoi, local news outlet Il Dolomiti noted. While Italian media cited her attempt to take a picture, the official alpine rescue logs noted only that she slipped at an exposed point on the mountain. Witnesses contacted emergency responders shortly before noon, The Daily Record reported. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER The 112 control center dispatched the Alta Val di Fassa team of the Trentino Alpine and Speleological Rescue Service, alongside an air ambulance, according to the Record. The woman lost her footing and fell an estimated 1, 000 feet down the slope. A mountain rescuer already in the vicinity went to the scene to provide the helicopter crew with exact coordinates, Italian regional news outlet Il Dolomiti reported. Medical personnel were lowered onto the mountainside by 12:30 p. m., where a doctor pronounced Rubio Leiva dead at the scene, according to Fox San Antonio. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Her family members were airlifted to the nearby town of Canazei, Il Dolomiti said. Her body was retrieved by helicopter and handed over to local authorities, News.com.au said. The Brigham Young University graduate worked as a manager for Rubio Contesse Advisors in Florida, according to Corriere della Sera, a major Italian newspaper. In recent months, the Dolomites have come under scrutiny for the massive crowds stretching through shuttle lines as visitors wait to reach Tre Cime di Lavaredo, one of the most iconic destinations. Viral videos have led to outrage online, with many commenters arguing that visitors were more interested in taking photos than enjoying the mountains, Fox News Digital previously reported. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Tre Cime di Lavaredo draws visitors from around the world with its trio of mountain peaks. The UNESCO-protected mountains are subject to the Enrosadira phenomenon, in which sunrise and sunset turn the rock walls a vibrant pink and orange, according to The Dolomites — UNESCO World Heritage Centre page. Tre Cime di Lavaredo gets over 800,000 visitors per year, per the Tre Cime di Lavaredo Hike Guide. Kelly McGreal of Fox News Digital contributed reporting.

articles.title: ‘Hid previous marriage’: Father accuses husband of murder after woman dies at Jhansi hotel
articles.summary: JHANSI: “After a month, she came to know that her husband had a previous wife who lives in Indore,” said the father of a 28-year-old woman who died after
articles.body: JHANSI: “After a month, she came to know that her husband had a previous wife who lives in Indore,” said the father of a 28-year-old woman who died after collapsing at a hotel in Jhansi. He accused her husband of murder, alleging that he had concealed his first marriage and frequently harassed her, according to news agency ANI.Speaking to the media, Muskan Simolia’s father, Ramji Lal Ahirwar, said, “I got my daughter Muskan married on June 29, 2026. After a month or so, she came to know that her husband had a previous wife who lives in Indore."“I watched the hotel CCTV footage, and it appears to me that he pushed her as soon as she entered the room. A person cannot fall so suddenly on their own,” Ahirwar added.“If someone is pushed, they would move their hands and legs or react in some way. He hit her with such force that it is evident how violently she was thrown,” Ahirwar said.“I am 100% suspicious because of his first wife. He would often harass my daughter, saying that his first wife was more beautiful and better than her, and that she and her father were worth nothing,” Ahirwar added.According to ASP Preeti Singh, “A woman was brought dead to the district hospital. Her husband was present with her and was questioned. He stated that he and his wife had stayed at Hotel Rishabh the previous night. While checking out today, they entered their room, and his wife suddenly collapsed.”“With the help of hotel staff, he took her to the hospital, where she was declared dead. CCTV footage was also examined, showing the woman entering the room with her husband and a hotel staff member. She is then seen collapsing while standing at the room’s threshold,” Singh said.“Afterwards, she was taken downstairs by her husband and hotel staff and rushed to the hospital. Further action will be taken based on the findings regarding the cause of death,” Singh added.Muskan died after collapsing near a hotel room’s doorway. CCTV footage reportedly shows her falling backwards moments after entering the room with her husband and a hotel staff member.Muskan was staying with her husband, Nilesh, a bank manager from Vidisha in Madhya Pradesh, at Hotel Rishabh in the Sipri Bazaar police station area. According to police, the couple checked into the hotel on Friday night. The following morning, Muskan was taken to the district hospital, where doctors declared her dead.The CCTV footage reportedly shows Muskan entering the room with Nilesh and a hotel employee. Within seconds, she collapses backwards near the doorway and hits her head on the ground. Nilesh is then seen lifting her and carrying her inside the room. She is later taken downstairs with the help of hotel staff and rushed to hospital.According to Nilesh, Muskan suddenly collapsed while the couple were preparing to check out. However, the circumstances surrounding her death remain unclear. The footage captures her fall but does not, by itself, establish what caused it or whether an assault took place.Ahirwar alleged that the family learnt about Nilesh’s first marriage after Muskan’s wedding and that the revelation led to frequent quarrels between the couple. He cited the alleged marital discord while questioning the circumstances surrounding his daughter’s death.Muskan had returned to her parental home in Jhansi on October 10 to prepare for a railway junior engineer examination scheduled for October 28, her father said. Ahirwar alleged that Nilesh arrived in Jhansi on October 23 and took Muskan with him on the pretext of visiting his aunt. He claimed that Nilesh instead took her to a hotel.Police have detained Nilesh for questioning as part of the investigation. The postmortem examination is expected to help establish the cause of death. articles.title: Ianto's shrine in Cardiff to Torchwood character to be 'regenerated'
articles.summary: Ianto's Shrine was removed from Mermaid Quay in Cardiff, but will be turned into a giant portrait.
articles.body:
A shrine for a much-loved character from Doctor Who spin-off show Torchwood has been given a new lease on life as a permanent artwork just months after being removed.

Fans who built the tribute to Ianto Jones in Cardiff 17 years ago were "devastated" in March when it was announced it would be taken down on health and safety grounds.

Now Cardiff-based artist Nathan Wyburn is turning all of the fan tributes into a giant portrait of the actor who played Ianto, Gareth David-Lloyd.

"I'm really pleased for [Torchwood fans] that it gets to live on," David-Lloyd told BBC Radio Wales Breakfast .

He said the Cardiff Bay shrine was "weird, but also very flattering and lovely".

Wyburn added he was "absolutely honoured to be the one entrusted with this".

"I knew as soon as the shrine was coming down that I had to do something. As a big fan of Torchwood myself the first time around, I've recently watched it all again as well."

Torchwood followed Captain Jack and his team of alien hunters and has grown a cult following among sci-fi fans since first airing in 2006.

Starring John Barrowman and Eve Myles, the BBC show has been praised for its LGBT representation, with pansexual character Jack, played by Barrowman, shown in a relationship with Ianto on primetime national television.

After Ianto was killed off in 2009, fans were quick to leave tributes at what became known as Ianto's Shrine in Mermaid Quay.

It had been looked after by Carol-Anne Hillman since 2017, who said she spent hundreds of pounds decorating it, with thousands of people from across the world coming to see it.

Wyburn said he was creating "a gigantic portrait" to be displayed at the nearby Red Dragon Centre "with the approval of Gareth himself" and the tribute materials given to him by Hillman.

"It's going to be an amazing piece. I cannot wait to unveil it to everyone," he said.

David-Lloyd said Wyburn had been "quite secretive" about his plans for the piece, adding he was "really pleased... it gets to live on".

"It's a bit bonkers, to be honest. I mean, I knew Ianto meant a lot to a lot of people, but the fact that he had a shrine for that amount of time that was maintained so meticulously, it was... a reminder of that special job that I did all those years ago."

A spokesperson for Mermaid Quay previously confirmed the shrine was being removed while maintenance work took place in the area, but added they wanted to "work with the local community" to create a new tribute to Ianto.

articles.title: Grudge report: Trump unloads on Norway over Nobel snub and imaginary triumphs
articles.summary: TOI correspondent from Washington: Hell hath no fury like Donald Trump scorned.
articles.body: TOI correspondent from Washington: Hell hath no fury like Donald Trump scorned. Norway has suddenly been reduced from a desirable source of immigrants to a “shithouse country”; comedian Bill Maher has received a 1,324-word dressing-down worthy of a bitter divorce petition. And somewhere in the increasingly tiresome presidential tirades, 11 downed aircraft and 30 million supposedly saved lives in the Indian subcontinent have made another fantasy-fuelled appearance.“Frankly, Norway sucks,” the MAGA boss announced at a Michigan rally on Sunday, before upgrading the insult to “Norway has become a shithouse country, actually.” The U.S President, who has made his not receiving a Nobel grievance a recurring feature of his political repertoire, explained his pique with the wounded dignity of a man who has been dumped by his girlfriend: “So I’m not in love with Norway,” he sniffed.Trump had denied that he had used the term “shithole country” against any nation, let alone Oslo, during his first term, but the gloves were off on Sunday as he put Norway in an expanding list of countries deemed insufficiently grateful, deferential, useful or impressed by him. At a rally in Georgia on Saturday, Trump had asked: “Why do we always have to take people from shithouse countries (like Somalia? Why can't we take people from, like, well, Norway, Sweden?” By Sunday, Norway had been demoted from immigration wish-list material to international pariah.Trump also invoked the May 2025 India-Pakistan conflict for about the 47th time, saying he had stopped the nuclear-armed nations from fighting. “They shot down 11 planes,” he told the Michigan crowd in another rambling speech, without explaining who shot down the planes. The MAGA boss’ recurring habit of reaching for impressive-sounding figures -- planes, lives, wars settled, tariffs, investments -- without providing any material to support them is now eliciting eye-rolls and shrugs both in the U.S and across the world with growing concerns about the fading of gravitas that is normally associated with the U.S Presidency.The Michigan rally also offered a reminder that the U.S President's digressions can go to uncharted territory, including sudden anatomical excursions. Having discussed international conflict and immigration, Trump turned to the Trinidadian rapper Nicki Minaj, a vocal supporter who appeared alongside him, to say, “By the way, I looked at one hell of a beautiful ass before, Nicki Minaj,” he announced. “That's hard to miss. Stand up.” Minaj rose and waved to the cheering MAGA audience.For those wondering if he had taken on the job of a casting direction in addition to that of a White House contractor, Trump explained that he was miffed with the “fake news” for misinterpreting his lingering description of Republican Senator Jon Husted’s physique, including his backside, legs, hands and neck, while admiring the former football player's athletic build. Trump’s admiration for the male anatomy is now the butt of jokes on the comedy circuit, but he apparently regards it as more than a joke of butts, a paean to the human body.The rally's more consequential rhetoric concerned Michigan's Democratic Senate candidate, Abdul El-Sayed, who could become the first Muslim elected to the Senate. Trump repeatedly called him a “jihadist”, invoked the September 11 attacks and portrayed his election as a national-security threat, while also suggesting Jewish Americans should be ashamed if they voted for him.The US President’s campaign rhetoric, regarded as “unhinged” by a growing number of commentators, was compounded on Sunday by a 1,324-word screed – his longest Truth Social post as per tracking databases – attacking the comedian Bill Maher as a “COMPLETE AND TOTAL LOSER,” ostensibly because Trump believed they had a good dinner meeting at the White House but Maher dumped on it on his HBO show.The MAGA boss complained about the show, its ratings, jokes and Maher’s supposed dishonesty, while threatening to have Republicans stop appearing on it, sounding less like a presidential critique than a breakup letter from someone who has discovered that a romantic dinner companion has subsequently made jokes at his expense. He also hinted in the tirade that he was considering moving the White House press corps from its long-established digs to make room for other uses.Numerous commentators worried about the tone, tenor, and digressions in Trump's campaign speeches, at a time the country is facing far more consequential issues than his construction projects, his relationship with a comedian or his not receiving the Nobel Prize, are starting to express concerns over the widening gulf between the gravity of the President's office and the material occupying the his attention. Former President Barack Obama summed it up during a rally over the weekend, saying, "These people are not serious."You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Exercise helps woman's confidence 'massively' after partying life
articles.summary: Megan Hamon says her life has turned around after struggling with excessive drinking and partying.
articles.body:
Meg Hamon was struggling with her self-confidence after she began to rely on partying and drinking to get by.

The problems began to develop during the Covid-19 pandemic and then continued until the start of this year when Hamon decided a change was needed as she was going to turn 30, she said.

Since then, she had focused on exercising through activities such as gym workouts and running, as well as going to therapy to improve her wellbeing, she added.

Hamon said: "Exercise has helped me massively with my confidence... If I'm ever feeling low, a good gym session will always help."

Hamon felt her problems had been growing for some time before she decided to take action to make a change in her life.

She said: "I think my lowest was Covid. I think that was like a struggle for everyone and I just had gone through quite a bad breakup.

"I was struggling with that and I just think I'd never really processed my emotion.

"I really neglected myself mentally and physically... but I just never really noticed how unhappy I was until I started to make a change."

Hamon said she had felt the benefits on focusing on her physical and mental wellbeing since making lifestyle changes.

She said: "Even if I had just done the therapy – it would be incredible... but I think the exercise side has just helped me massively with my confidence."

Hamon has been sharing her experiences on social media as well, adding : "If it inspires one person to make a change, then I think it's really important to do that as well.

"If you get stuck in the same cycle... I just think you can find so many other things to do than going out and just drinking excessively."

Hamon has been going to therapist Sally Agathangelou as part of her work to improve her wellbeing.

Agathangelou said: "It could be various issues, it can be drinking, it can be gambling, it can be drugs, it can be self-harm - but it's all bridges for coping."

"I'm really quite proud of this generation because they are very open to therapy," she added.

"I'm very, very proud of them because I can support, but it's down to them at the end of the day to make that change."

articles.title: Independent review announced into murder of student Henry Nowak
articles.summary: "We must get to truth of what happened before, during and after that awful night," the home secretary says while announcing the review.
articles.body:
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has announced an independent review into the murder of Henry Nowak.

The 18-year-old student was fatally stabbed in Southampton in December by Vickrum Digwa, who falsely claimed he had been racially abused and had acted in self-defence. Digwa was jailed for life on 1 June, with a minimum term of 21 years.

Following the teenager's murder, police bodycam footage of him being handcuffed as he lay dying led to intense scrutiny of the Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary and sparked wider debates around knife laws, race, policing and public trust.

The review, which was welcomed by Nowak's family, will be led by former Justice Secretary Alex Chalk KC.

"We must get to truth of what happened before, during and after that awful night and we must do everything in our power to ensure that no family suffers the same fate," Mahmood told the House of Commons on Monday.

Mahmood said the review will investigate what was known about Nowak's killer and if there were missed opportunities to intervene as well as the treatment of his family in the justice system and whether they received enough support.

In a statement published on Monday, the Home Office said the review will be carried out in two parts.

Phase one will cover the police, health services, local authorities educational institutions and faith organisations, including if any concerns were raised relating to weapon possession and violent behavior, the statement said.

It will also look to determine if there were missed opportunities to prevent Nowak's murder.

Phase two will follow after the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) has concluded its investigation into the actions of police officers who attended the scene.

It will consider the actions of the IOPC and "if necessary" the police, the Home Office added.

The IOPC launched its own investigation into the response on the night of Nowak's death after bodycam footage showed the 18-year-old was handcuffed and left dying on the floor despite informing officers of his injuries.

The investigation was launched despite a sentencing judge ruling Nowak would not have survived his injuries, however quickly he received treatment.

The Nowak family described the announcement as a "significant moment in our fight for justice."

"We hope this review, alongside the ongoing investigations and inquest, will finally uncover the full truth and deliver the accountability and meaningful change we have fought so hard for," they added in a statement.

"Our experience of the criminal justice system has been deeply disappointing, and we are determined that no other family should have to endure what we have."

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch welcomed the decision to launch the review.

"There must be proper accountability for those who failed Henry and his family," she said.

The review is due to report in five months.

Nowak, from Chafford Hundred in Essex, was a first-year accountancy and finance student at the University of Southampton when he was murdered.

On the night of Nowak's muder, it was Digwa's brother who called 999, claiming Vickrum had been attacked "racially".

Bodycam footage released by Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary, with the permission of Nowak's family, showed officers speaking to Digwa and others while Nowak lay on the ground.

Nowak could be heard repeatedly saying that he had been stabbed and could not breathe.

Violent disorder broke out in Southampton in the days following the release of the footage.

After Digwa's sentencing, Nowak's father Mark called for a "full, fearless and transparent" investigation into the police response.

But he also urged people not to use his son's death to "create further division, hatred or tension".

articles.title: Brazil election: How 'Lula's Army' WhatsApp channel helped turn race around
articles.summary: Millions joined a 'Lula's Army' channel that helped to transform online enthusiasm into real-world mobilisation.
articles.body:
A WhatsApp channel created to support Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's re-election campaign is being credited by allies with helping deliver one of the most unlikely comebacks in recent Brazilian politics.

Brazil's left-wing president had been trailing right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro, but managed to turn the race around in just three weeks.

At a moment when many doubted Lula could reverse the result, a WhatsApp channel called Lula's Army emerged, and rapidly grew to 10.8 million followers.

Led by Congressman André Janones, the operation encouraged supporters to share videos, promote hashtags and recruit new voters.

Its dramatic growth between the two rounds was particularly notable because it appeared to reverse a long-standing imbalance in Brazilian politics.

For years, conservatives aligned with former President Jair Bolsonaro had been widely seen as dominating online political mobilisation, especially on platforms such as WhatsApp and Telegram.

The emergence of Lula's Army convinced many supporters that Brazil's left had finally found a way to compete in a digital arena. The shift was particularly significant because social media has played a central role in Brazilian politics since Jair Bolsonaro's 2018 election victory, when WhatsApp networks became a defining feature of political campaigning.

Lula's Army messages often included ready-made templates for followers to share with friends and family. Each one assigned supporters a specific task aimed at boosting Lula's visibility on social media.

Janones frequently instructed his "troops" to "blow up" the latest campaign video or help a new hashtag "take off".

"Guys, urgent!", "Don't go to sleep yet", "No food before the mission!", and "I have one more task before you're dismissed", were some of the instructions.

On the eve of the election, the congressman also hosted a 24-hour live event - dubbed the "turnaround livestream" - even as polls continued to suggest a victory for Bolsonaro.

The tactic worked, despite worries by some members of the Workers' Party that Janones's often-confrontational style on social media could undermine the more moderate image they hoped to project for Lula.

In his victory speech, Lula referred to Janones as "our General" and thanked him for "raising the morale of our troops every day".

Measuring the electoral impact of online mobilisation, however, is notoriously difficult.

While Lula's allies credit Lula's Army with helping fuel the comeback, political scientists caution that it is impossible to determine how many votes, if any, were directly influenced by the WhatsApp operation.

Political scientist Denilde Holzhacker argues that a shift in Lula's campaign strategy was key to his comeback.

Rather than relying solely on online engagement, she says the Workers' Party candidate succeeded in connecting digital campaigning with grassroots mobilisation on the ground.

According to Holzhacker, the campaign intensified local efforts and adapted its messaging - linking a Bolsonaro victory with concerns about potential changes to social programmes and the loss of rights.

"It was to Lula's credit that he recognised his own weakness and completely changed his style," she says. "And Janones managed to do something that had seemed unthinkable for Brazil's left - dominate social media."

By contrast, Holzhacker argues that Flávio Bolsonaro entered the run-off overly confident of victory and failed to communicate his message to his supporters as effectively.

Sociologist and political scientist Mayra Goulart, a professor at the Federal University of Rio de Janeiro, also cautions against attributing Lula's comeback solely to social media.

"It was a combination of social media and street-level mobilisation," she says. "The physical world enabled a form of mobilisation capable of reducing abstention and persuading undecided voters."

In her view, Lula's supporters succeeded in turning online enthusiasm into real-world political engagement.

"Those committed to Lula's victory worked to bring people together and persuade them to vote," Goulart says.

She argues that the effort not only helped increase turnout but could also prove valuable for Lula's next administration.

"I believe this collective effort was an important learning experience and will prove valuable for a government that still faces many battles ahead. It not only helped reduce abstention, but also converted a significant number of undecided voters."

Lula himself suggested that the mobilisation behind his comeback could shape the way he governs in the years ahead.

In his victory speech, he said the election had taught him many lessons and pledged to change the way Brazil is governed.

"We are going to give people a greater say in decision-making, and digital communication will play a much bigger role in my government."

articles.title: Israel committing crimes against humanity in occupied West Bank: UN
articles.summary: UN report highlights crimes including extermination, torture, rape and other forms of sexual violence.
articles.body:
Israel has committed crimes against humanity, including “extermination”, in the occupied West Bank, United Nations-mandated investigators have reported.

The UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory said on Monday that the Israeli government and its forces are also responsible for other war crimes and crimes against humanity in the Palestinian territory, including torture, rape and other forms of sexual violence.

The release of the report came as Israeli forces carried out a clampdown , including expulsions and home demolitions, in Hebron following a gun attack last week.

The commission, which does not speak for the UN itself, first determined in a September 2025 report that Israel had committed “genocide” in its war on Gaza. That followed Hamas’s deadly October 7, 2023 attack on Israel – Israel flatly rejects the finding.

In its new report, issued the day before Israel’s general election , the commission found that in the West Bank – which Israel has occupied since 1967 – Israeli military operations , reinforced by sustained settler violence, constitute a “widespread and systematic attack” against civilians.

“The Israeli authorities and forces have committed the crimes against humanity of extermination, torture, rape and other forms of sexual violence in the West Bank, as well as persecution based on intersecting discriminatory grounds, with nationality, race and ethnicity at its core,” it said.

Israel’s mission in Geneva said the report was part of the inquiry’s “misinformation campaign to demonise the State of Israel and portray its very existence as criminal”.

“The international community must reject these distortions, repudiate the commission’s findings and demand its immediate dissolution,” the mission said in a statement.

The three-member UN investigative team was established by the UN Human Rights Council in 2021.

Former South African High Court judge Navi Pillay, who chaired the investigation until last November, won the Nobel Peace Prize earlier this month.

The commission’s new report is focused on killings and bodily and mental harm caused by both Israeli and Palestinian security forces since October 2023.

It found that the situation in the occupied West Bank has deteriorated gravely since the Palestinian armed group Hamas’s attack from Gaza that month.

The commission found that the Israeli authorities “intended to collectively punish” West Bank civilians due to the Hamas attack.

Israel’s military offensive on Gaza has displaced nearly the entire population of Gaza and killed at least 74,500 people, according to Gaza’s Health Ministry.

According to the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, between October 7, 2023 and October 9 this year, 1,143 Palestinians – at least 250 of them children – were killed in the West Bank, including occupied East Jerusalem.

Later on Monday, the UN Human Rights Commissioner, Volker Turk, condemned the ongoing Israeli operation in the West Bank city of Hebron , saying threats to empty and erase neighbourhoods raise “serious concerns of ethnic cleansing”.

Israeli forces imposed a lockdown across Hebron on Friday following the gun attack near the city, and Israeli Prime Minister, Benjamin Netanyahu announced plans to lock down the entire West Bank .

Turk’s statement noted that the lockdown has already resulted in the forcible displacement of over 2,000 Palestinians, the demolition of homes and the prevention of residents from moving freely.

“The sweeping steps taken raise grave concerns of unnecessary and disproportionate use of force – which must end,” he said.

“The Israeli lockdown is confining many to their homes and their immediate neighbourhoods. Declarations by senior Israeli government officials indicate that the measures implemented are punitive in nature and designed to instil fear. This is unacceptable,” Turk added.

Israeli ministers have previously called for the occupied West Bank and Gaza to be ethnically cleansed.

Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich said in an interview with the news outlet Ynet News last month that Israel should “go to war” in the occupied territory and repeat what it “did in Gaza”.

He added that Israeli forces had “cleared out” Palestinian refugee camps in the West Bank.

Since Israel launched its genocidal war on Gaza, arrest campaigns have increased in the West Bank, with settler pogroms also continuing. The government is encouraging the expansion of settlements, which are illegal under international law, despite a backlash from some Western officials.

Turk insisted that people displaced under the clampdown must be allowed to return home and that “Israel must ensure compensation and reparation for unlawful evictions and demolitions”.

“Collective punishment is a grave violation of international law,” he said.

articles.title: Police arrest teenager after shooting that injured 12, including children, in Florida
articles.summary: The incident happened on Saturday night, close to an American football stadium where a game had just been played.
articles.body:
Police have arrested a teenager in connection with a shooting on Saturday that injured 12 people in Florida.

The incident took place at 20:00 local time (01:00 Sunday GMT), close to an American football stadium in the city of Tallahassee where a university game had recently been played.

Eleven people were injured by gunfire, local police said, while another hurt their ankle while fleeing the scene. Six of the victims were children.

Anthony Rivers III, 15, has been charged with 11 counts of attempted second-degree murder and possession of a firearm by a delinquent.

Police said the shooting followed an altercation between people who knew each other and that additional arrests were possible.

None of the victims appear to have been the intended targets, they said in a statement.

"What should have been a weekend of celebration in our community instead became a night of fear and violence for the victims and their families," Tallahassee Police Chief Lawrence Revell said.

"We remain committed to holding those responsible accountable and getting answers for every family impacted by this tragedy."

Police said on Sunday that six people were in hospital, including one person who was in a critical condition. Five people had been released.

Revell told a press conference on Sunday that police had had to carry victims in their arms to get them to emergency responders because of the crowds from the football game.

articles.title: Tributes paid to man killed by falling tree in Storm Boelo
articles.summary: Richard Baines was the long-serving curator of Logan Botanic Garden near Stranraer.
articles.body:
Tributes have been paid to a man who died after being hit by a falling tree in Dumfries and Galloway.

Richard Baines, 60, the long-serving curator of Logan Botanic Garden near Stranraer, died during Storm Boelo on Sunday morning .

It is understood that he was walking near his home in Mid Kelton, just outside Castle Douglas, when the accident happened.

David Knott, director of horticulture at the Royal Botanic Garden in Edinburgh, said they were "desperately sad, devastated" by the news.

"He had a warmth, a genuine sense of humour, he always made time for individuals and that's one of the tributes that has been said many times this morning," Knott told BBC Scotland News.

"He always found time for his colleagues. And he was always very supportive in providing opportunities for the next generation of horticulturalists. He was a very genuine and warm human being."

Logan Botanic Garden is home to a range of exotic plants as it benefits from the warming influence of the Gulf Stream. It is one of four Scottish gardens run by the Royal Botanic Garden in Edinburgh.

Knott said Baines came up with the description of Logan as " Scotland's most exotic garden " and worked hard to promote both the garden and the south-west of Scotland.

Knott said his colleague would be remembered for his "passion and enthusiasm for plants" and for significantly expanding the plant collection at Logan.

During his tenure, he was primarily responsible for significant developments including the first public conservatory to be powered by green energy in the UK.

Baines also participated and led fieldwork in China, the Canary Islands and Vietnam, from where seven plant species new to science were catalogued.

"Richard's contribution as an enthusiastic plantsman and curator at Logan and to the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh's wider work and culture has been immeasurable, and he will be deeply missed by many," Knott said.

Dumfries and Galloway MSP Finlay Carson also paid tribute to Baines, a former school friend.

"Richard was a remarkable gentleman and a good friend to many, always ready with a warm smile, a kind word and an infectious enthusiasm for life," he said.

The Scottish Conservative MSP said that Baines' work at Logan Botanic Garden had earned him national recognition.

"His expertise, commitment and achievements brought credit not only to his profession but to Galloway as well," he added.

Baines died as Storm Boelo swept across Scotland, causing flooding, travel disruption and power cuts over the weekend and into Monday.

The wind picked up on Saturday and an amber warning was in place from Saturday night.

Galloway Mountain Rescue Team (GMRT) said they had responded to "one of the most gruelling callouts our team had faced in recent history" on Saturday.

They were called to Curleywee in the Minigaff Hills to help a runner who was injured while taking part in the OMM mountain challenge.

In a post on Facebook , they said 10 members of their team pushed through "torrential rain, severe wind and unforgiving boggy ground" to reach the casualty.

A coastguard helicopter had to turn back due to the deteriorating weather.

The team said they had to carry the casualty off the hill, with the help of members of the OMM safety team, before handing the runner to the Scottish Ambulance Service.

OMM has faced some criticism on social media for allowing the run to go ahead in the poor weather.

A spokesperson said the course was closed and all competitors accounted for before the amber wind warning took effect at 21:00 on Saturday.

"The event team continually assessed the mountain weather forecast in the build-up to and throughout the event, with competitor safety guiding every decision," they added.

The spokesperson said they were grateful for the "understanding and support" shown as the event was adapted to the forecast conditions.

They said they would be making as a donation to GMRT, as is usual practice at OMM events whether or not a callout takes place.

articles.body: President Donald Trump set social media ablaze on Sunday night with a lengthy Truth Social post slamming HBO host Bill Maher on the heels of a recent dinner between the two of them, leaving onlookers baffled at the sudden about-face. Trump hosted Maher for dinner at the White House earlier this month, marking the second time they have dined together. Afterward, Trump told reporters that the HBO comedian was "great," and that it "was a very informative dinner," but the president changed his tune on Sunday night. "Let’s talk about this COMPLETE AND TOTAL LOSER, Bill Maher. He’s got a Low Rated Show on equally Low Rated HBO, which was once, long ago, a Network of Quality and Excitement — But that’s all gone. It’s not 'HOT' anymore!" Trump wrote. Trump also described his past relationship with Maher's "Club Random" show producer Chuck LaBella from his days on NBC's "The Apprentice," claiming that LaBella would frequently encourage Trump to appear on Maher's show. BILL MAHER CLAIMS DONALD TRUMP FELT 'BETRAYED' BY HIM WITH 'SILLY' FEUD AFTER CORDIAL 2025 DINNER "When I became President, I agreed to meet, after the first one, and the last one, but never agreed to do his show, which he wants me to do, DESPARATELY [sic] — It won’t happen! When I have watched the show, which isn’t often, it always ends with dishonesty, about me at least, but, who cares?" Trump wrote. articles.title: LA mayoral hopeful Nithya Raman calls herself both a 'capitalist' and 'democratic socialist'
articles.summary: Nithya Raman called herself both a capitalist and a democratic socialist on CNN, drawing sharp criticism as the DSA considers challenging her endorsement.
articles.body: Los Angeles mayoral candidate Nithya Raman declared herself both a capitalist and a democratic socialist during an interview Friday, raising questions about her political ideology as the Democratic Socialists of America considers challenging her endorsement from the organization just days before the election. Raman, a Los Angeles city councilwoman and DSA member challenging incumbent Mayor Karen Bass, defended the two labels when Michaelson pressed her about capitalism and the organization's political positions. "I am a capitalist, and I'm also a democratic socialist," she told CNN's Elex Michaelson. "I want the city to work and when the government is doing its job, it needs to work really effectively, and we need to make sure capitalism works without harm to workers, without worker exploitation, without exploitation of poor people. That's what I'm going to focus on." Los Angeles County Republican Party Chair Roxanne Hoge criticized Raman's remarks in a statement to Fox News Digital, questioning how the mayoral hopeful could embrace capitalism while maintaining ties to an organization that advocates replacing it. DEPROGRAMMED: FORMER DSA INSIDER REVEALS ‘FRIGHTENING’ SOCIALIST AGENDA DROVE HIM FROM ‘EXTREME’ IDEOLOGY "It's no surprise that Nithya Raman is confused by two mutually exclusive concepts. Perhaps she was in a fugue state when she agreed to co-govern with the DSA who proudly proclaim their desire to expropriate private property and to abolish the police," Hoge said. The Los Angeles Times reported Saturday that DSA national leadership was considering action against the Los Angeles chapter's endorsement of Raman over accusations she doesn't fully support the Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions (BDS) movement targeting Israel. At a forum last month, according to the LA Times, Raman referred to BDS as a "legitimate form of peaceful protest" without explicitly saying she supports the movement. Lisa Cusack, president of the Don't LA My Burbank PAC, criticized Raman's affiliation with the Democratic Socialists of America, pointing to the organization's communist roots and its current political program advocating greater worker control over private industries. "The founder of DSA-LA, Dorothy Rea Healey, was a longtime leader of the California Communist Party in California," she told Fox News Digital. "Her autobiography is titled: 'A Life in the American Communist Party.' The current Democrat Socialist Program for Los Angeles states, 'Capitalists extract massive profits by stealing the surplus value of working-class labor.'" She claimed the program's mantra involves organizing to rebuild worker militancy, expanding union density, dismantling the gig economy, and asserting democratic worker control over municipal and private industries. "This is who Nithya Raman will be expected to co-govern with. When people tell you who they are, believe them," Hoge said. 'DSA JIHADI': LA MAYORAL CANDIDATE TORCHED AFTER DEFENDING 'GENOCIDE' COMMENT DURING JEWISH FORUM Raman's remarks contrasted with the DSA's official description of democratic socialism, which calls for replacing capitalism with an economic system in which workers exercise greater control over businesses and major industries. The organization explicitly rejects capitalism in its explanation of its political philosophy. "Capitalism is a system designed by the owning class to exploit the rest of us for their own profit. We must replace it with democratic socialism, a system where ordinary people have a real voice in our workplaces, neighborhoods, and society," the DSA states on its website. DNC CHAIR KEN MARTIN DEFENDS 'BIG TENT' STRATEGY WHEN PRESSED ON DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS Raman's latest comments also marked a change from how she answered the same question during a July interview with Michaelson. At the time, she declined to directly identify herself as a capitalist, instead emphasizing the existing economic system and the responsibilities of local government. When Michaelson asked whether she considered herself a capitalist, Raman acknowledged the economic structure under which Los Angeles operates. "You know, we are in a capitalist system. It's a city government," Raman said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE Michaelson also asked Raman whether she supported abolishing police departments, prisons or the U.S. Senate. She rejected all three proposals. When Michaelson pressed her on how she reconciled her political affiliations with those disagreements, Raman defended the ideological diversity within the organization. "I don't, you know, I think democratic socialism is a big tent," she said. "The DSA is a big tent organization, and I'm in part of that tent and I think a lot of Angelenos are in that tent with me." articles.title: The best methods (and products) for cleaning wooden kitchen utensils and prevent splintering
articles.summary: These are the best methods for cleaning stained, old wooden utensils, like spoons and spatulas, to make them look new again.
articles.body: You probably have at least a few wooden spoons and spatulas in your kitchen that you’ve had for a few years. While you may clean them regularly, you likely also find that some of them just don’t seem to ever truly get clean, particularly if they’re stained from some sort of seasoning or food. While wooden kitchen utensils are a great alternative to toxic black plastic utensils, they require a little more care to help them last. I spoke to multiple cleaning experts to learn how to clean wooden kitchen utensils and accessories, like spoons, cutting boards, spatulas and more. Below, they share the best methods for getting rid of stains and smells, and how to actually keep your utensils clean over time. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best products for cleaning wooden kitchen utensils Before you can get to the steps for cleaning your utensils, you’ll need to gather your supplies, like the ones below. The picks on this list are highly reviewed and have at least a four-star rating from 500 or more shoppers on Amazon and/or are direct recommendations from our staff of wooden utensils users. This food-safe mineral oil is free of fragrances or smells and it’s safe to use on kitchen utensils made from all different types of wood, as well as other products made from bamboo, according to the brand. While you can use it for many different types of wooden kitchen utensils, the brand recommends it mainly for cleaning and moisturizing wooden cutting boards, butcher blocks and even some non-wooden surfaces like a stainless steel oven or fridge. Plus, shoppers say that it’s easy to apply (you simply add some of the oil to a kitchen towel and rub into the surface) and doesn’t leave a sticky feeling behind. If you want an entirely new set of utensils to start with, this set is a great place to start; each piece is BPA-free and the set includes a mix of spoons and spatulas made from teak wood, as well as a holder to keep them all in one place and a wooden spoon rest for when you’re cooking. It also comes with metal hooks so that you can hang them using the small loops on the handles of the spoons and spatulas. You can get a set with six, eight or 10 pieces, and a popular cutting board set. Dawn’s popular Powerwash Dish Spray is one of my most recommended products because it’s so versatile and great for washing dishes of all materials without accidentally overusing the soap. This starter kit comes with one spray bottle and three refills. It’s great for cleaning wooden kitchen utensils without leaving a strong fragrance (this spray has a nice clean yet not abrasive smell to it). Additionally, the brand recommends using it to clean other surfaces like stainless steel appliances and even some clothing. To clean, dry and oil your wooden kitchen utensils, you should get a set of kitchen cloths or towels like these. The towels are available in several sizes and they have a waffle-like (honeycomb) texture that helps them absorb moisture and dry fast, according to the brand. Shoppers say the towels are absorbent and feel soft. I love using Scrub Daddy (and Scrub Mommy) sponges to clean all of my dishes, but particularly dishes and utensils that food tends to adhere to a lot. When I use these sponges, they do a great job of wiping crusty food residue from utensils, but they’re also effective at cleaning oil and grease from pans, plates and more. You do have to use a lot of water to make them usable and squeezable, but they also last a long time compared to traditional kitchen sponges. How to clean wooden kitchen utensils For things like wooden spoons, spatulas and cutting boards, it’s important to make sure that you dry them just as thoroughly as you wash them, according to Robin Murphy, a cleaning expert and chief cleaning officer at home cleaning company Maid Brigade. Make sure to use warm water, dish soap and a sponge or soft brush to clean them thoroughly. “Wash them after use, rinse well, and dry them with a clean towel,” she says. “Let them air-dry completely before putting them away. If the wood starts looking dry, condition it with a little food-grade mineral oil.” Additionally, it’s important to use a brush or sponge to clean wooden kitchen utensils to help clean in between crevices and grooves on wooden surfaces, according to Kadi Dulude, cleaning expert and owner of home cleaning company Wizard of Homes. “Use a little bit of mild dish soap and a sponge/brush to remove all food residue, paying attention to get into grooves and joints too,” she says. “Then rinse well and air dry. Don’t put them flat on a wet cloth or anywhere air isn’t circulating, or mold and mildew will grow.” Here are your step-by-step instructions from the experts: After using your wooden spoon, spatula, cutting board or other wooden kitchen utensil, immediately rinse it with warm water to get rid of residue. Don’t put it in the dishwasher. Apply warm water and a small amount of mild dish soap, such as Dawn Platinum Powerwash Dish Spray, to a sponge, soft brush or Scrub Daddy, and use it to gently scrub the surface of your wooden spoon, spatula or cutting board, focusing on the surfaces and ends that touch food. Rinse them thoroughly with warm water, pat them dry with a paper towel or kitchen towel, and then place them on a drying rack, so that they’re completely exposed to air and therefore dry as fast as possible (don’t place them flat on a kitchen towel, for example).For old wooden utensils that are dry and faded, both Murphy and Dulude recommend using a food-grade mineral oil meant for conditioning wooden accessories, such as Kate Naturals Mineral Oil for Wood Cutting Boards. When the wooden utensils are completely dry, apply a small amount of the mineral oil to a cloth and rub the oil onto the surface of it. Allow the utensil to dry completely before storing or using it. Can you put wooden utensils in the dishwasher? Both Murphy and Dulude recommend not washing wooden kitchen utensils in the dishwasher (even if the label says it’s dishwasher safe) because the process can be very harsh on the surface of the utensils. “The dishwasher gets too hot and it’s not good for wood to sit in a hot humid environment for too long. It will cause your items to warp or split” says Dulude. “Some utensils may be safe for the dishwasher, but if you really want to prolong their life, handwash them.” Additionally, water expands as it dries which leads to wooden kitchen utensils cracking and splintering, according to Murphy. How to maintain wooden kitchen utensils As I mentioned above, Murphy and Dulude recommend using a mineral oil to help maintain wooden kitchen utensils. A food-grade mineral oil helps restore the moisture in wooden spoons, spatulas and cutting boards without giving them an oily feeling or making foods oily. It’s similar to seasoning a cast-iron skillet or using a moisturizing cream on your face to help restore your natural skin barrier. When should you replace wooden kitchen utensils? Pay attention to the surface of the wooden utensil and see if it’s damaged or rough. “Once you start seeing deep cracks it’s time to stop using it because food and moisture will get into the cracks which can contaminate [the next] food [you’re preparing],” says Dulude. “If it’s just [a] small imperfection or roughness then there’s hope you can save it by lightly sanding and using food-grade mineral oil.” What products should you not use on wooden kitchen utensils and why? You should avoid harsh cleaning products, like pure bleach or abrasive cleaners, like powders or pastes, because they can mess up the surface of the wood, according to Murphy. She also says to avoid using things like vegetable or olive oil because they become rancid over time, which is why food-safe mineral oil is best. This is also a reminder as to why cleaning them thoroughly is important since they probably already come in contact with things like vegetable and olive oil via cooking and food prep. We also take steps to ensure all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and without undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. Robin Murphy is a cleaning expert, chief cleaning officer at home cleaning company Maid Brigade and writer at cleaning site Who Likes It Dirty.Kadi Dulude is a cleaning expert and owner of home cleaning company Wizard of Homes Why trust NBC Selected? I’ve written about how to clean hardwood floors and stainless steel appliances and the best shower cleaning products. For this story, I spoke to multiple cleaning experts for their guidance and recommendations. articles.title: Ethiopia attacks: More than 60 Orthodox Christians killed in Oromia
articles.summary: One resident, whose 75-year-old father was killed, described it as an ambush, saying they were surrounded.
articles.body:
More than 60 people have been killed in a series of attacks on Christians in Ethiopia's Oromia region, according to the country's Orthodox Church.

One resident, whose 75-year-old father was killed, described it as an ambush. "We were completely unprepared and had no prior knowledge. They surrounded us from all four directions," he told BBC Amharic.

The regional government said that it would take action against those responsible.

A local official blamed the attacks on a newly formed rebel coalition, the Alliance for Survival, which includes the Oromo Liberation Army (OLA). The OLA has not commented but has denied carrying out previous such attacks.

A statement from the Holy Synod of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church said that 20 houses were burnt to the ground in the attacks. It did not say who was responsible.

Eyewitness told BBC Amharic that five of those killed were children.

A church official described the attacks on three areas in the Shirka district as a "massacre", saying security forces arrived at the scene but were unable to stop the assault.

Condemning the violence, the Orthodox Church said attacks against Christians had been increasing recently, and that "such actions undermine the country's values of mutual respect and peaceful coexistence".

In a statement posted on Facebook, the Orthodox Church said it had repeatedly raised concerns about insecurity with authorities at different levels of government, but that "so far there has been no solution".

The Ethiopian Human Rights Council, a non-governmental organisation, said in a report released in July 2026 that 458 people had been killed in attacks in that area over the previous four years.

But this is one of the most deadly attacks in that period.

The report said armed groups had repeatedly targeted local communities, particularly followers of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church, in what it described as religiously motivated attacks.

The government has previously blamed the OLA for the attacks, with Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed saying violence targeting civilians and religious institutions was part of a plan to destabilise the country.

The group, which says it is fighting for greater rights for the Oromo people, denies these allegations.

Previous reports have also documented attacks against Muslims in the area. Residents who spoke to the BBC on various occasions have described the violence as both ethnic and religious in nature.

About two-thirds of Ethiopians are Christians, mostly Orthodox, while one third are Muslim.

articles.title: In 2020, Jeff Robertson turned his Halloween skeleton display into a $1.1 million fundraiser for St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital; now, 625 homes aim to raise $2 million in 2026
articles.summary: What started as an elaborate Halloween decoration in North Carolina has grown into a nationwide fundraising movement, with 625 households across the
articles.body: What started as an elaborate Halloween decoration in North Carolina has grown into a nationwide fundraising movement, with 625 households across the United States expected to participate in 2026. Retired Army veteran Jeff Robertson, who launched Skeletons for St. Jude in 2020, is now hoping the initiative will reach its ambitious target of raising $2 million for St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital.Robertson, from Holly Springs, North Carolina, initially attracted attention for his elaborate Halloween yard display, which featured an army of skeletons. His decorations became so popular that horror fans travelled for hours to see them. But instead of keeping the spotlight on his family, Robertson decided to use the attention to support children receiving medical treatment.“That night we had a family huddle and said, ‘This is kind of cool that we’re on the news, but you know, let’s kind of take the spotlight off of us,” Robertson told St. Jude Inspire. “Like, how can we use this for good?”The family agreed to start a fundraiser for St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital. That decision gave rise to Skeletons for St. Jude, which has raised more than $1.1 million in its first six years.Jeff Robertson’s Halloween tradition now includes 625 homesWhat began as one family’s effort has expanded into a nationwide campaign involving hundreds of Halloween enthusiasts, commonly known as “haunters”. Participants decorate their homes with skeletons, animatronics, tombstones and other spooky attractions, inviting visitors to enjoy the displays while contributing to the fundraiser.In 2026, the initiative is expected to bring together 625 households across the US. A week before Halloween, 202 participating households had already registered their addresses on the online “Fright Map”, helping visitors locate participating homes and plan their visits.The fundraising season extends beyond Halloween, continuing through December 25. This allows participating families to use their seasonal displays to raise donations and awareness for the hospital throughout the holiday period.The campaign’s message encourages people to take part without giving up the Halloween traditions they already enjoy.“Same haunt you already build. Way bigger reason,” the initiative said in a statement.Skeletons for St. Jude sets $2 million fundraising target for 2026Now in its seventh year, Skeletons for St. Jude has set its sights on raising $2 million in total donations by the end of 2026. The campaign also aims to raise more than $100,000 during the 2026 Halloween and holiday seasons.The organisers have thanked the volunteers and participating households who have helped turn Robertson’s idea into a nationwide initiative.“Thank you to all of our team members who have made Jeff’s dream more than a reality!” the organisation said on its website.It also encouraged more people to join the campaign and use their Halloween displays to draw attention to the children being treated at St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital.The hospital’s mission is central to the fundraiser. St. Jude says families do not receive bills for treatment, travel, housing or food, helping them focus on their children during an extremely difficult time.From 40 animatronics to a 12-foot flaming skeletonThe participating homes have developed their own creative ways of attracting visitors and encouraging donations.In Grand Rapids, Michigan, Jeffery Broking spent October setting up a display at his grandmother’s house, installing more than 40 animatronics. For him, the fundraiser has a personal connection. He told WDIO ABC that he has been dealing with seizures over the past few years and has met several sick children and their families.“I just want to give back,” Broking said.In Willits, California, participant Krystle Coffman had a 12-foot flaming skeleton on her lawn, with safety measures in place. She told local reporter Kym Kemp that visitors could also expect candy and other surprises.“We will be handing out candy and may have a few special surprises,” Coffman said.Meanwhile, Elizabeth Stripling was building her display in Delmar, Maryland, decorating her lawn and her neighbour’s property with skeletons, pumpkins, tombstones and spiderwebs.Stripling said she was already decorating for Halloween when she learnt about the initiative and decided to participate. Joining the fundraiser gave her an additional reason to expand her collection while bringing happiness to children in her neighbourhood.“The more I learned about it, I thought, why not?” she told news station WMDT. “I’m already decorating and I’ve already got skeletons, so I’ll just go ahead and gives me an excuse to build to my collection. And it brings such joy to the kids in the neighborhood.”Why the campaign is about more than HalloweenFor Stripling, who serves as the director of outreach and training at the Kennedy Krieger Institute’s Center for Autism Services, the initiative is also about remembering children who may be spending Halloween in hospital instead of celebrating with their families.“We think a lot about kids at Halloween. And that’s what Saint Jude is all about. It’s all about kids,” she said.She explained that the displays could bring a little happiness to children receiving treatment, reminding them that people outside the hospital are thinking about them during the festive season.“They’re not feeling well if they’re there in the hospital and ... this is something that might bring them a little light too, to know that there are people out here thinking about them on Halloween night, wishing they could be celebrating with them.”You use AI every day. articles.body: A federal judge ruled on Monday (local time) that the Trump administration’s dismissal of Maurene Comey, daughter of former FBI director James Comey, from her post as a federal prosecutor was unlawful.Judge Jesse M Furman rejected the Trump administration’s argument that the dismissal was valid on the grounds that federal prosecutors exercise the president’s “conclusive and preclusive” powers.“The court concludes the defendants are wrong,” the judge wrote.Furman rejected the administration’s argument that Congress cannot regulate the removal of federal prosecutors, saying the claim “flies in the face of nearly two centuries of Supreme Court precedent.”“Indeed, to accept Defendants’ argument would be to unsettle the very equilibrium established by this Nation’s constitutional system," the judge added.Maurene Comey was dismissed from her position as an assistant US attorney in July last year, after serving in the role for a decade. The court noted that she had worked on some of the country’s most high-profile cases and had consistently received “the highest accolades from supervisors and peers alike.”Following her dismissal, she sued the Justice Department and other officials, alleging that her termination violated the constitutional separation of powers, the First Amendment and the Fifth Amendment’s Due Process Clause.Maurene Comey alleged that she was fired because she is the daughter of James Comey, a longtime critic of President Donald Trump, or because of her perceived political affiliations and beliefs.A Barack Obama appointee, James Comey served as FBI director from September 2013 until May 2017, when he was dismissed by Trump, during the Republican's first White House term.(With AP inputs)You use AI every day.
